en.g: Asia, a province of the Roman Empire in western Anatolia

1000170.etyen:
Derived from Latin Asia, from Ancient Greek Ἀσία (Asía). The Greek name originally referred to Anatolia and other lands east of the Aegean Sea, and was subsequently used for the Roman province of Asia in western Anatolia before being extended to the continent as a whole.
The name is often connected with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀯𐀹𐀊 (a-si-wi-ja) and Hittite Aššuwa, the name of a region or confederation in western Anatolia. An alternative proposal connects it with a Semitic word asu, meaning “east” or “sunrise”, but the ultimate origin is uncertain.
Compare Danish Asien, Swedish Asien, German Asien, Ice

1000426.etyen:
Derived from Old Norse Eyvindr. The modern form was revived as a historical-literary name during the Nordic name renaissance in the mid-19th century.
The Old Norse name continues *Auja-winduʀ, traditionally analysed as containing an element related to *awją (“luck, good fortune”) and the name element *-winduʀ (“victor, victorious lord”), although the precise origin and interpretation of the elements remain somewhat uncertain.
Doublet of Even (“male given name”), the inherited Norwegian continuation of the same Old Norse name.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Eivind, Faroese Eivindur, Danish Ejvind an
